A URL containing a single quote (legal in URLs) escapes the single-quoted href attribute, and since the post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (cook returns raw unmodified), the injected markup becomes live HTML rendered via `raw post.cooked` in embed/best.html.erb. The mechanism is fully verifiable in the diff.

judged_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:13 interpolates `url` unescaped into a single-quoted href after only a prefix check (`url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`); URLs legally containing a single quote (e.g. slugs like `/it's-alive.html`) terminate the attribute early and corrupt the stored HTML, and a crafted feed link such as `http://host/x' onmouseover='...` performs attribute injection that lands as live markup since the post is raw_html-cooked (second XSS path).

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the diff appends `"#{url}"` into `contents` after only checking `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`. This does not prevent legal URLs containing a single quote or other attribute-breaking characters, so `href='...` can be terminated early and additional attributes/handlers injected. Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unchanged, and the embed view renders with `raw post.cooked`, the injected HTML would be served as live markup (XSS/markup corruption).
